questions.questionText: By what percentage did the auction price rise from 2019 to 2024? (Correct to one decimal place.)
questions.shortcut: Change ÷ original × 100.

questions.questionText: Revenue = production × auction price. What was the revenue in 2023? (in ₹ lakh)
questions.shortcut: Lakh × rupees gives rupees in lakh directly.

questions.questionText: Revenue = production × auction price. In how many of the 6 years was the revenue above the average revenue of all 6 years?
questions.shortcut: Compute the mean once and compare each product.

questions.questionText: Revenue = production × auction price. By what percentage did the revenue change from 2019 to 2024? (Correct to one decimal place; give the magnitude.)
questions.shortcut: Do not add the quantity and price growth rates; multiply the factors.

questions.questionText: Revenue = production × auction price. Find the ratio of the revenue in the year of the highest auction price to the revenue in the year of the lowest auction price. (Give as a decimal correct to two decimal places.)
questions.shortcut: Pick the two years from the line first, then bring in the quantities from the table.

questions.questionText: What is the average selling price over the 6 years? (₹ per litre, correct to one decimal place)
questions.shortcut: Read the line points and take a simple mean.

questions.questionText: By what percentage did the selling price rise from 2018-19 to 2023-24? (Correct to one decimal place.)
questions.shortcut: Change ÷ original × 100.

questions.questionText: Revenue = milk sales × selling price. In which year was the revenue the highest?
questions.shortcut: The year of highest price or highest quantity need not give the highest product.

questions.questionText: Revenue = milk sales × selling price. In how many of the 6 years was the revenue above the average revenue of all 6 years?
questions.shortcut: Compute the mean once and compare each product.

questions.questionText: Revenue = milk sales × selling price. The revenue of the first three years is what percentage of the total revenue of all six years? (Correct to one decimal place.)
questions.shortcut: Total revenue = sum of the six products; use it as the base.

questions.questionText: Revenue = bricks supplied × price. Find the ratio of the revenue in the year of the highest price to the revenue in the year of the lowest price. (Give as a decimal correct to two decimal places.)
questions.explanation: Highest price in 2024: 54×10 = 540. Lowest price in 2019: 30×6 = 180. Ratio = 540 ÷ 180 = 3.00.
questions.shortcut: Pick the two years from the line first, then bring in the quantities from the table.
